summary: SSE JSON-RPC messages split across events after CDN re-write, causing malformed partial outputs
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent malformed partial JSON-RPC responses delivered over SSE. The client receives SSE events that contain fragments of a single JSON-RPC message split across two or more events; the client JSON parser errors with 'Unexpected end of JSON input' and the streamed choice is discarded. This occurs only when traffic flows through the customer's CDN/edge (Cloudflare) with Accept-Encoding: gzip set by the client.

Impact:
- NarrativeAI sees ~1-3% of user sessions end with partial/malformed streamed responses for long outputs (>4KB).
- Behavior is reproducible for long responses and during bursts; short responses unaffected.
- Customer currently on Dedicated tier; affects production traffic in us-east.

Environment:
- Customer: NarrativeAI (dedicated)
- Route: /v1/stream/generate -> hosted edge-proxy (Cloudflare) -> api-gateway -> serving-runtime
- Model: open-instruct-3b (pinned)
- Client: browser client with Accept-Encoding: gzip; HTTP/2 to CDN

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Establish SSE connection to /v1/stream/generate with standard stream params and Authorization header.
2) Send a prompt that results in large multi-kB streaming output (e.g., long bullet list).
3) Observe SSE event sequence in HAR or tcpdump; client reports JSON parse errors on a fraction of sessions.

Observed behavior (example log fragment):
--- sse-fragments.log ---
[event id=123]
data: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":42,"result":{"choices":[{"text":"Once upon a time, in a remote valley, the people"}\n\n[event id=124]
data: ", often gathered for the harvest. They would sing songs and tell stories of the old"\n\n[event id=125]
data: " days.\n"\n--- end ---\nClient-side error: SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input at JSON.parse (<anonymous>)

Notes: the JSON object above is split mid-string across event boundaries. The split is byte-aligned and does not correlate with logical token boundaries. The customer attached a HAR showing the CDN returning frames that appear to insert or coalesce chunk boundaries.

Immediate customer workaround requested: customer tried switching to websockets and saw no errors; also verified that setting Accept-Encoding: identity at client eliminates the issue (no gzip).
comments: 2026-03-13 10:12 - Asha Patel (Support): Logged initial report from NarrativeAI. Requesting HAR, SSE transcript, and sample prompt. Notified SRE due to CDN involvement.
2026-03-13 11:04 - NarrativeAI (Customer): Uploaded HAR and sse-fragments.log. Repro rate ~1.8% during peak. Note: happens only with gzip enabled on client.

2026-03-13 12:30 - Priya Rao (SRE): Reproduced locally by proxying through a Cloudflare worker that performs gzip re-write. Observed chunk boundaries inserted at compression flush points; SSE event boundaries not preserved by our framing when the edge re-chunks response bytes.

2026-03-13 13:05 - Liam Chen (Engineer): Experimented with adding Cache-Control: no-transform and checking Transfer-Encoding behavior. Local emulation with no-transform prevented the CDN worker from re-writing; replication rate dropped to 0% in test.

2026-03-13 14:20 - Support (Asha): Sent temporary workaround to customer: set Accept-Encoding: identity or use websocket transport. Customer acknowledged workaround reduces errors but asks for a platform solution.

2026-03-14 09:10 - Liam Chen (Engineer): Opening PR to edge-proxy to set Cache-Control: no-transform for SSE routes and ensure server flushes SSE events in single write() calls. Related PRs: https://github.com/redwood/edge-proxy/pull/4821

2026-03-14 11:35 - Priya Rao (SRE): Noted that some CDNs still buffer despite no-transform; we will add a header signal 'X-SSE-Event: 1' for edge-config to bypass compression layer for known SSE routes.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Combination of CDN/edge worker compression and downstream HTTP/2 framing causes chunks to be re-chunked at arbitrary byte boundaries. Our SSE framing assumes that when the server writes a logical event it will arrive as contiguous bytes; edge re-write introduces split chunks containing partial JSON strings. Reproducer: client -> Cloudflare worker that performs gzip re-encode with intermediate flush; when worker flushes, the gzip block boundary sometimes lands inside a JSON string and the worker emits chunk boundary which the client perceives as SSE event boundary. Verified by toggling Accept-Encoding and simulating worker behavior. Priority: P1 because dedicated customer production errors. Next steps: land edge-proxy change to add Cache-Control: no-transform on SSE endpoints and add signal header for CDN rules to bypass compression; add server-side write semantics to ensure event lines are emitted in single syscall where possible.
resolution_notes: Workaround provided to customer: (1) Set Accept-Encoding: identity in client, or (2) switch to websocket transport for long outputs. Platform mitigation in progress: PR to edge-proxy to set Cache-Control: no-transform for SSE routes (PR #4821) and an accompanying small change in realtime-proxy to emit SSE events using a single write() per event. SRE to coordinate with CDN partner to add rule to bypass gzip for routes with 'X-SSE-Event: 1'. Estimated roll-out: edge config change + CDN rule within 72 hours after PR merge. Follow-up: add automated test that simulates gzip re-chunking and checks JSON integrity across SSE events.
